status: open qualification questions retained; assigned analysis complete

items.finding: No retrieved SA, CVD SiC, reaction-bonded SiC or SiC/SiC population supplies matched compression m, characteristic strength, effective reference size and confidence bounds for finished P3 members.
items.needed: Raw compression failures, specimen and stress-field dimensions, processing/batch information, fracture modes, fit method, competing populations and confidence bounds; evidence of transfer to full curved tubes.
items.effect: Qualified compression parameters and actual member/frame Pf remain null. Catalogue 3.9 GPa is only a typical value; hypothetical scale assignments do not qualify it.

items.topic: Integer frame and resolved member loads
items.finding: CHECK-022d uses continuum count 432.9863. Rounding to 433 does not define a closed triangular mesh; 435 is only a compatible counting example. The three independently recovered 026b meshes use different geometries.
items.needed: A physically specified selected integer mesh, all section properties, boundary conditions, member forces and nonlinear load paths.
items.effect: 433-member probabilities are risk bookkeeping. The selected-point joint-moment estimate is a dimensional sensitivity, not an equilibrium solution.

items.finding: The source's approximately 44.19 kg CFRP joining estimate and 44.02 mm overlap do not establish rotation, contact, adhesive peel, end damage or statistical reliability for roughly 866 end interfaces.
items.needed: Joint geometry and stiffness, local contact and bond stresses, combined-load tests, processing variability, failure distributions, environmental durability and allocation of joint risk.
items.effect: The tube-only risk budget omits an unresolved system contribution. The proxy moment is not a physical bound.

items.finding: Nominal beam normal stresses are compressive, but ideal beam shear produces small positive principal-stress estimates. Hoop stresses, pressure load path, membrane attachment, contact and residual stresses are not resolved.
items.needed: Validated three-dimensional joint/member stress fields and a suitable multiaxial fracture law, including tensile surface/volume flaw populations.
items.effect: Zero longitudinal tension cannot be reported as zero actual tensile or frame hazard. Uniform tensile levels and stressed fractions are sensitivity inputs.

items.topic: Flexure reference sizes and statistical meanings
items.finding: SA sources report m=10 and m=8; catalogue 380 MPa is typical rather than explicitly a fitted mean. Bend spans are absent. Commercial CVD reports m=11, scale 424 MPa and mean 415 MPa but no specimen dimensions.
items.needed: Applicable product revision, specimen spans and orientation, sample sizes, raw data, finish, fit definition and uncertainty. Clarify the CVD mean/scale relationship without replacing the reported scale.
items.effect: SA 40/20 mm spans and mean-to-scale conversions remain PROJECTION. Commercial CVD has no justified full-size probability here.

items.finding: The 2017 paper's labelled effective bend volume equals the 360 mm3 span prism. The normalized stress-power integral at m=8.6 instead gives 1.953125 mm3. Ring values likewise need stress-field interpretation.
items.needed: Reconcile the paper's geometric definitions and size-transfer convention with its full stress field and flaw populations before transferring its fitted data.
items.effect: Our explicitly defined three-point projection is retained; ring geometric sizes are not used as uniform tensile reference volumes.

items.topic: SiC/SiC population, size and source consistency
items.finding: Mini-composite tensile gauge area is missing. The pilot appendix's specimen labels and stated strength range need reconciliation; the scale table header has a unit inconsistency. The compression study uses a different 2.5D architecture and only three coupons.
items.needed: Gauge area, full raw data, corrected labels/range/units, fitting details, anisotropic failure mechanisms and matched full-component compression/tension statistics.
items.effect: Reported tensile batch m/scale values are preserved separately, not combined with the 460 MPa compression mean or monolithic weakest-link scaling.

items.finding: The owner reports large rise-8 moments and tensile stresses. The old independent 026b run was refused admission and produced no independently verified rise-8 force solution.
items.needed: An admitted independent geometry/load-path solution and verification, plus a separately defined selected-point rise case if transfer is intended.
items.effect: Owner rise-8 stresses remain attributed and unverified. Applying the same moment to another section is only a section conversion. No refusal was bypassed or retried for this card.

items.finding: The selected tube is approximately 3.184 m long, 275.083 mm OD and 1.137 mm wall. Its L/1000 initial bow is an assumed imperfection, not a measured tolerance distribution or the spherical centerline curvature.
items.needed: Demonstrated fabrication capability, full-length section/bow measurements, surface and end preparation, machining/handling damage controls and strength data at this size.
items.effect: Current catalogue properties cannot establish the delivered-member lower tail. The actual material improvement factor remains unknown.

items.finding: The source's 1.258252 stability multiplier is not a failure-probability distribution. No new nonlinear FE equilibrium or first-loss solve was performed here.
items.needed: Validated local/global instability, joint interaction, imperfection and fracture models with their uncertainties for the same actual design.
items.effect: Strength improvements and conditional tube Pf do not qualify stability. Linear target scaling of frozen 026b stresses is only a sensitivity.

items.finding: The 433-member targets allocate probabilities near 2.31e-6 and 2.31e-9 per member, well below the empirical resolution of the retrieved small samples.
items.needed: Physically justified tail extrapolation, parameter confidence bounds, competing failure populations, batch effects and validated proof-screen modelling.
items.effect: Point-estimate Weibull projections are not confidence-qualified reliability predictions. Zero-failure sample counts are illustrative, not a proposed testing campaign.

items.finding: Service duration, cycles, environment, slow crack growth and post-proof damage are unspecified.
items.needed: Defined lifetime/load spectrum and matched environmental growth, aging, handling and fatigue evidence.
items.effect: Lifetime failure probability remains null. Ideal instantaneous proof truncation cannot establish lifetime survival.

items.finding: The illustrative 1.25-times-target axial proof is 1.374281 MN, with pressure-equivalent multiplier 1.572816 exceeding the source's stability multiplier. Support, confinement and local loading can change which flaws are screened.
items.needed: Validated fixture, proof stress coverage and load sequence, instrumentation and inspection sensitivity, proof-damage assessment, handling limits, accept/reject criteria and subsequent life model.
items.effect: PROOF.md is a prospective qualification outline, not a ready test protocol. Proof rejection rate and residual reliability are unknown.

items.finding: Headline targets allocate the entire risk budget to tube fracture and use an independent series model. Joints, membrane, instability, shared batches and common-cause events are omitted.
items.needed: A whole-frame failure definition and allocated risk budget; valid component marginals and dependence/common-cause model.
items.effect: The conditional series probabilities are not whole-vehicle reliability claims. Union-bound allocations avoid independence but do not supply missing marginal probabilities.

items.topic: Closest qualified grade and improvement route
items.finding: SA is the closest catalogue compression comparison in the retrieved set, but no candidate is qualified for this geometry and target tail. CVD and CMC datasets describe different populations and modes.
items.needed: Matched full-member comparisons and evidence that strength, scatter or validated screening can deliver the required combined-stress lower quantile.
items.effect: The conditional 2.24427-times 3.9 GPa requirement at m=10 is not an established improvement factor over today's delivered SiC.

items.finding: Geometry, loads, complete inspection and proof coverage imply high/custom qualification and recurring inspection cost classes, but no supplier quotation or process yield is available.
items.needed: Supplier capability and quotations, fixture design, throughput, inspection detection performance, scrap rate and surveillance plan for the qualified process.
items.effect: No dollar estimate, cycle time or scrap forecast is asserted. No supplier contact or purchase was made.
